fix: bundle libgcc_s.1.1.dylib for Intel builds

The resolve_rpath function was only searching /opt/homebrew/Cellar
but Intel Macs use /usr/local/Cellar. Now searches both locations.

Fixes #879

fix: use shell redirection for PlistBuddy Delete commands

Homebrew's formula `system` method doesn't support Ruby's `err:`
keyword argument. Replace `err: File::NULL` with shell redirection
`2>/dev/null || true` to suppress errors when CFBundleIconName
doesn't exist.

Fixes #881

Fix tree-sitter compatibility for Emacs 29 and 30

Replace ts_language_version with ts_language_abi_version to support newer
tree-sitter versions that removed the deprecated function.

- Add treesit-compatibility.patch for Emacs 29 and 30
- Apply patches conditionally when tree-sitter option is enabled
- Use local_patch method for proper integration

Based on commit c27c6f37126fd6045983ce91aa4118b42849d6f2 from
daviderestivo/homebrew-emacs-head

fix: always apply treesit-compatibility patch

The patch was conditional on `build.with? "tree-sitter"` but there's
no such option - tree-sitter is a hard dependency. Apply the patch
unconditionally since it works with both tree-sitter 0.25 and 0.26+.

Also update CI to use tree-sitter (0.26+) instead of tree-sitter@0.25.

Revert "fix: always apply treesit-compatibility patch"

This reverts commit 0dfce51c482581b1694edb9166a13994da5fcd65.

feat: update dependency from tree-sitter@0.25 to tree-sitter

- Change depends_on to use tree-sitter (0.26+) instead of tree-sitter@0.25
- Apply treesit-compatibility patch unconditionally
- Fix patch header (was incorrectly referencing .orig file)
- Update CI to use tree-sitter instead of tree-sitter@0.25

docs: add cask installation documentation

- Add 'Pre-built binaries (Cask)' section to README
- Add cask build badge to header
- Update table of contents
- Add NEWS entry for cask support

fix: add retry logic for concurrent cask updates

When both release(30) and release(31) run simultaneously, they can
race on pushing to master. Add exponential backoff retry loop.

fix: generate dSYM bundle when using --with-debug

On macOS with clang, debug symbols are stored in .o files and the
executable only contains references to them. Homebrew cleans up temp
files before dsymutil can extract the symbols.

Run dsymutil after make install to generate the .dSYM bundle with
actual debug symbols that debuggers can use.

Fixes #362

fix: enable debug symbols properly with Homebrew's superenv

The --with-debug option was not producing usable debug symbols because
Homebrew's superenv shim filters out -g and -O flags from compiler
command lines and replaces them with its own defaults.

Changes:
- Use ENV.set_debug_symbols to tell Homebrew's superenv to add -g flag
- Move dsymutil to run BEFORE gmake install (needs access to .o files)
- Run dsymutil on source path before installation
- Simplify CFLAGS handling - let superenv handle optimization/debug flags

This is the proper Homebrew way to enable debug symbols without using
env :std which disables superenv entirely and makes builds more fragile.

Fixes #362

fix: rename dSYM to match binary name for lldb auto-discovery

The wrapper script renames Emacs to Emacs-real, but the dSYM was still
named Emacs.dSYM. This caused lldb to not auto-find the debug symbols.

Now the dSYM is renamed to Emacs-real.dSYM after installation, so lldb
can automatically discover it without manual `target symbols add`.

Only applies to @29, @30, @31 which use inject_path (wrapper script
that renames the binary). @27 and @28 use a simpler wrapper that
doesn't rename the binary.

fix: apply treesit-compatibility patch in CI workflow

The workflow was updated to use tree-sitter 0.26+ but the
treesit-compatibility patch was not added to the PATCHES array,
causing builds to fail with 'undeclared function ts_language_version'
errors.

fix: regenerate info dir file in post_install

Homebrew's cleaning phase deletes the `dir` file created by `make install`.
This fix ensures the `dir` file is regenerated in `post_install` by running
`install-info` for each info file.

Changes:
- @27, @28: Add missing install-info post_install code
- @29, @30, @31: Fix glob pattern to match both .info and .info.gz files
  (for users with --with-compress-install)

Fixes #437

refactor: split CI jobs by Emacs version for independent releases

Previously, if Emacs 30 failed to build, Emacs 31 cask would not be
released because the release job depended on all build matrix jobs.

Now each version has its own independent pipeline:
- build-30 → release-30
- build-31 → release-31

This ensures that a failure in one version does not block releases
of the other version.

chore: deprecate --with-imagemagick option in @31

Modern Emacs has native support for most image formats:
- SVG via librsvg
- WebP (native in Emacs 30+)
- PNG, JPEG, GIF (built-in)

ImageMagick adds complexity and can cause issues (delegate failures,
PATH problems from GUI). Adding deprecation warning to gauge usage
before removal.

fix: apply treesit-compatibility patch unconditionally for Emacs 29

The patch was conditional on 'build.with? "tree-sitter"' but tree-sitter
is a required dependency, not an option. This caused the patch to not be
applied, breaking builds with tree-sitter 0.26+.

feat: add ns-emacs-plus-version variable for detection

Adds `ns-emacs-plus-version` constant that allows users to detect
Emacs Plus in their init.el:

  (when (bound-and-true-p ns-emacs-plus-version)
    ;; Emacs Plus specific configuration
    )

Implementation:
- Creates site-start.el in Emacs.app/Contents/Resources/site-lisp/
- Wrapper script prepends this to EMACSLOADPATH so it loads first
- Only enabled for @30 and @31

Closes #599

revert: pin tree-sitter back to 0.25 for Emacs 29 and 30

The tree-sitter 0.26+ compatibility patches don't fully resolve the
API incompatibility issues. Reverting to tree-sitter@0.25 which is
known to work correctly with Emacs 29 and 30.

Ref: https://github.com/d12frosted/homebrew-emacs-plus/issues/854

docs: add ns-emacs-plus-version and other updates

- Document ns-emacs-plus-version for detecting Emacs Plus in init.el
- Add deprecation notice for --with-imagemagick in @31
- Document info dir file fix

feat: add script to generate Tahoe Assets.car for icons

Adds `scripts/generate-tahoe-assets` utility for icon contributors to
generate macOS 26 Tahoe-compatible Assets.car files from PNG sources.

Usage:
  ./scripts/generate-tahoe-assets <png-file> [output-dir]
  ./scripts/generate-tahoe-assets community/icons/<name>

The script:
- Creates a temporary .icon bundle with icon.json configuration
- Compiles it with actool to generate Assets.car
- Works with both raw PNG files and community icon directories

Salvaged from #852 and adapted for single-icon processing.

fix: set PKG_CONFIG_PATH for keg-only tree-sitter@0.25 in CI

tree-sitter@0.25 is keg-only and not linked to standard paths,
so configure couldn't find it. Adding PKG_CONFIG_PATH to resolve.

feat: re-apply icon from build.yml during post_install

Adds `apply_icon_post_install` function that allows quick icon testing
without a full rebuild. Run `brew postinstall emacs-plus@31` to apply
the icon configured in ~/.config/emacs-plus/build.yml.

This is useful for:
- Testing icon changes without rebuilding Emacs
- Quickly switching between icons
- Verifying Tahoe Assets.car installation

Also adds re-signing of Emacs Client.app in post_install.

feat: show Tahoe-compliant icons at top of gallery

Updates the icon gallery generator to:
- Detect icons with Assets.car (Tahoe-compliant)
- Display Tahoe-compliant icons in a separate section at the top
- Explain "icon jail" for standard icons on macOS 26+

Currently only liquid-glass has proper Tahoe support.

feat: add dragon-plus icon with Tahoe liquid glass support

A proper macOS 26 Tahoe icon created with Icon Composer, featuring
layered design with gradients and translucency effects that display
natively without "icon jail".

Includes Assets.car for Tahoe and icon.icns for backwards compatibility.

feat: add Tahoe icon sources and light/dark preview variants

- Add icon.icon source bundles for dragon-plus and liquid-glass
- Generate preview-light.png and preview-dark.png for Tahoe icons
- Update gallery to show Light/Dark columns for Tahoe icons
- Update generate-icon-previews.rb to use ictool for Tahoe previews
- Change example icon to dragon-plus in documentation

feat: add shared IconApplier for formula and cask icon support

- Add Library/BuildConfig.rb for parsing build.yml and resolving icons
- Add Library/IconApplier.rb for applying icons to Emacs.app
- Update EmacsBase.rb to use IconApplier in post_install
- Update casks to apply custom icons from build.yml in postflight

This enables cask users to customize icons via ~/.config/emacs-plus/build.yml
just like formula users. To apply an icon after changing build.yml:
  brew reinstall --cask emacs-plus@31
fix: correct SHA256 for arm64-26 cask build
fix: remove ctags binary symlink (not in build)

fix(ci): properly update SHA256 values in cask files

The previous approach tried to replace placeholders (PLACEHOLDER_ARM64_26)
that didn't exist in the cask files. The sed replacement failed silently,
leaving old SHA values while only updating the version number.

Now uses Python to find each URL pattern (e.g., arm64-26.zip) and updates
the SHA256 on the preceding line, which matches the actual cask structure.
fix(ci): use python3 -c instead of heredoc to avoid YAML parsing issues
fix(ci): move SHA update logic to external Python script
docs(icons): clarify that icon customization works for both formula and cask

fix(ci): only build Emacs 30 cask on manual trigger, not nightly

Emacs 30 is a stable release built from a tarball, not git master.
Nightly rebuilds are wasteful since the source rarely changes.
Only Emacs 31 (master branch) needs nightly builds.

fix(ci): smart triggers for stable vs development builds

- Emacs 30 (stable): build on formula/patch/Library changes, not nightly
- Emacs 31 (development): build nightly from master branch
- Both: can still be triggered manually

This avoids wasteful nightly rebuilds of stable releases while keeping
development builds up-to-date with upstream changes.

fix: move mac-font-use-typo-metrics patch to community opt-in

The patch was causing issues with some fonts (e.g., PragmataPro) where
English text had excessively low line height. While the patch fixes CJK
rendering issues in vterm, it's not universally beneficial.

Users who need this patch can now opt-in via build.yml:

  patches:
    - mac-font-use-typo-metrics

Ref #864
docs: add README for mac-font-use-typo-metrics patch
docs: clarify when to use mac-font-use-typo-metrics patch

feat(cask): add native compilation environment injection

Inject LSEnvironment into Emacs.app Info.plist during cask postflight
to enable native compilation when launching from Finder/Dock.

Sets PATH, CC (gcc-15), and LIBRARY_PATH (including libemutls_w location)
so libgccjit can find gcc and its libraries without requiring users to
configure their shell environment.

Can be disabled via ~/.config/emacs-plus/build.yml:
  native_comp_env: false

Fixes #837

docs: add Build Configuration section

Document build.yml options including:
- icon: custom icon selection
- native_comp_env: environment injection for cask native compilation

This provides a central place for build configuration documentation
and explains how cask users can control the native compilation
environment injection.
docs: add patches and revision to build.yml options

fix(cask): create CLI wrapper for proper bundle path resolution

When running `emacs` via the Homebrew symlink, Emacs couldn't find its
bundle resources because argv[0] was the symlink path, not the real
binary path.

This creates a wrapper script at Emacs.app/Contents/MacOS/bin/emacs
that uses the absolute path to exec the real Emacs binary. The cask
now symlinks to this wrapper instead of directly to the binary.

Fixes #885

fix(cask): create emacs symlink in postflight after wrapper exists

The binary stanza for emacs was failing because it runs before
postflight, but the wrapper script at MacOS/bin/emacs is created
in postflight by CaskEnv.inject().

Move the emacs symlink creation to postflight (after the wrapper
is created) and add uninstall_postflight to clean it up.

Fixes the "symlink source is not there" error on clean install.

fix(cask): add libgccjit dependency for native compilation

Native compilation requires libgccjit at runtime to compile trampolines
and JIT-compile Elisp code. Without it, users see "library 'emutls_w'
not found" and "error invoking gcc driver" errors.

fix(cask): also depend on gcc for libemutls_w.a

libgccjit and gcc are separate Homebrew formulas. libgccjit provides
the JIT library, but gcc provides the toolchain and runtime libraries
like libemutls_w.a that libgccjit needs to actually compile code.

docs: improve documentation accuracy

- Fix cask macOS version support: ARM64 13+, Intel 15+
- Add note explaining cask build availability per architecture
- Document HOMEBREW_EMACS_PLUS_BUILD_CONFIG env var
- Document EMACS_PLUS_NO_PATH_INJECTION env var
- Document fallback config path ~/.emacs-plus-build.yml
- Remove --with-no-frame-refocus from Emacs 30/31 (not needed)
- Remove --with-imagemagick from Emacs 31 docs (deprecated)

refactor: remove --with-no-frame-refocus option from Emacs 30/31

This option is no longer needed since the same behavior can be achieved
natively in Emacs 29+ using:

  (add-to-list 'default-frame-alist '(undecorated . t))

refactor: remove deprecated --with-X-icon options, unify icon handling

This commit removes the deprecated --with-X-icon options from all formulas
and unifies icon handling between cask and formula installations.

Changes:
- Remove Library/Icons.rb (ICONS_CONFIG no longer needed)
- Remove scripts/migrate-icons.rb (one-time migration completed)
- Remove inject_icon_options method from EmacsBase.rb
- Remove check_deprecated_icon_option method from EmacsBase.rb
- Remove ICONS_CONFIG fallback in resolve_registry_icon
- Update all formulas (26-31) to use build.yml for icons
- Update validate-icons.rb to validate against community registry

Both cask and formula now use the same unified icon path:
  build.yml -> community registry -> apply_custom_icon/IconApplier

All 77 icons remain available via build.yml configuration.

chore: remove legacy icons directory

- Remove icons/ directory (95MB of duplicate .icns files)
- Remove unused icon_url method from UrlResolver.rb

All icons are now served from community/icons/ with metadata.

refactor: rename casks to emacs-plus-app, add @master aliases

Cask naming:
- emacs-plus@30 → emacs-plus-app (stable)
- emacs-plus@31 → emacs-plus-app@master (development)

Formula alias:
- emacs-plus@master → emacs-plus@31

This naming scheme:
- Follows homebrew-core convention (emacs vs emacs-app)
- Uses semantic names (@master) instead of version numbers for casks
- Simplifies upgrades: stable users just use emacs-plus-app regardless
  of which Emacs version is current

docs: update NEWS with 2026-01-05 changes

- Cask renamed to emacs-plus-app / emacs-plus-app@master
- New emacs-plus@master formula alias
- Removed --with-no-frame-refocus option
- Removed deprecated --with-X-icon options
- Removed legacy icons directory

docs: simplify README install section

- Put casks (pre-built) first as the easy/fast option
- Consolidate formula examples under "Build from source"
- Remove verbose version list from intro
docs: move screenshot below install commands
fix(ci): update cask file paths in commit step
fix(ci): use new --with-icon= syntax in nightly workflow
fix(ci): remove deprecated icon test from nightly workflow

fix(ci): add missing CFLAGS and flags to cask builds for formula parity

Add build flags that were present in the formula but missing from the
cask workflow, causing LSP/eglot issues due to low file descriptor limits:

- Add CFLAGS: -DFD_SETSIZE=10000 -DDARWIN_UNLIMITED_SELECT
- Add configure flags: --with-rsvg, --with-webp
- Add webp dependency to brew install

Fixes #889

fix(ci): remove ImageMagick from cask builds to fix libomp conflict

ImageMagick links against libomp.dylib for OpenMP parallelization.
When bundled into the cask, this conflicts with the system's libomp
loaded by gcc/libgccjit at runtime, causing "OMP: Error #15:
Initializing libomp.dylib, but found libomp.dylib already initialized"
crashes when entering dired-mode.

ImageMagick is optional in the formula anyway, so users who need it
can build from source with --with-imagemagick.

Fixes #890

fix: call super in CopyDownloadStrategy to set @url

Homebrew's new concurrent download UI calls #url on download strategies
to display progress. CopyDownloadStrategy was overriding initialize
without calling super, leaving @url nil and causing "Expected type
String, got type NilClass" errors during patch downloads.

Fixes #891

fix(ci): build Emacs 30 cask from release tag, not branch

The cask was building from the emacs-30 branch HEAD, resulting in
version 30.2.50 instead of 30.2. Now uses the emacs-30.2 release tag.

Fixes #892

fix: use applet.icns for Emacs Client.app icon

Emacs Client.app is an AppleScript app which uses applet.icns,
not Emacs.icns. The IconApplier was copying to the wrong filename.

Fixes #893

docs(readme): Add build from source and Centaur Emacs links

Added new instructions for building from source (Formula) and
included a link to Centaur Emacs as an inspiring project.

fix: add build.yml validation with helpful error messages

Addresses #896 - users now get clear error messages instead of cryptic
Ruby errors like "undefined method 'key?' for an instance of String"
when their build.yml has syntax issues.

Changes:
- Add BuildConfig::ConfigurationError with descriptive messages
- Validate YAML structure (must be a hash, not string/array)
- Reject unknown keys with typo suggestions (Levenshtein distance)
- Validate all config keys: icon, patches, revision, native_comp_env
- Add context-specific warnings (e.g., patches ignored in cask builds)
- Add verbose config output when loading build.yml
- Add 42 tests covering all validation cases
- Update CI to run all test files

Example error for "icon:foo" (missing space):
  Invalid build.yml at /path/build.yml
  Expected a YAML mapping (key: value pairs), but got: String
  Common causes:
    - Missing space after colon (use 'icon: value' not 'icon:value')

Example error for typo "icons: dragon-plus":
  Unknown configuration key(s): icons
  Valid keys are: icon, patches, revision, native_comp_env
  Did you mean:
    - 'icons' -> 'icon'

refactor: consolidate config loading in BuildConfig module

- EmacsBase now delegates to BuildConfig for config loading, validation,
  registry access, and maintainer formatting
- Removed ~70 lines of duplicated code from EmacsBase
- Fixed constant redefinition warnings in UrlResolver using defined? guard
- revision_from_config silently ignores errors (shown later during build)

This ensures formula and cask use the same validation logic.

refactor: replace build script with Makefile

Replace the simple ./build shell script with a Makefile that provides:
- make test: run all unit tests
- make validate: validate build.yml configuration
- make formula-XX: build formula (e.g., make formula-31 --HEAD)
- make cask / make cask@master: test local cask changes
- make postinstall-formula: simulate formula post_install
- make postinstall-cask: simulate cask postflight

The cask targets temporarily modify the tap's cask file to use local
Library/ code, then restore the original after installation.

Add helper scripts for postinstall simulation:
- scripts/postinstall-formula.rb
- scripts/postinstall-cask.rb

docs: update local build instructions to use Makefile

Replace references to ./build script with make targets in:
- docs/development-guidelines.org
- scripts/create-community-patch.rb

fix: include ns-emacs-plus-version in cask builds

Add site-start.el with ns-emacs-plus-version to cask builds, matching
the formula post_install behavior. This allows users to detect Emacs
Plus in their init.el:

  (when (bound-and-true-p ns-emacs-plus-version)
    ;; Emacs Plus specific configuration)

Fixes #895

feat: add inject_path option for PATH injection in formula builds

Add configurable user PATH injection for formula builds. This addresses
the common issue where GUI Emacs doesn't have access to user's shell PATH.

Key discovery: macOS blocks PATH in LSEnvironment for security reasons,
while allowing other env vars like CC and LIBRARY_PATH.

Solution: Store the desired PATH in a custom env var (EMACS_PLUS_PATH)
via LSEnvironment, then have site-start.el read it at Emacs startup to
set exec-path and process-environment.

Formula builds:
- Full user PATH captured via ORIGINAL_PATHS (set by Homebrew)
- ns-emacs-plus-injected-path is t when PATH was injected
- Configurable via inject_path option in build.yml (default: true)

Cask builds:
- PATH injection is NOT available (Homebrew limitation)
- Cask postflight runs in controlled environment without user's PATH
- ns-emacs-plus-injected-path is always nil for cask
- Native compilation works via CC and LIBRARY_PATH
- Users should use exec-path-from-shell or switch to formula

Breaking changes:
- Removed EMACS_PLUS_NO_PATH_INJECTION environment variable
- Replaced native_comp_env option with inject_path in build.yml
docs: add pre-Tahoe compatibility notes for Tahoe icons

fix(emacs-plus@31): add libgen.h for basename() on macOS 26

Emacs commit bc5fb19 (Jan 17, 2026) added a call to basename() in
src/pdumper.c without including <libgen.h>. On macOS 26 (Tahoe), this
causes a build failure as basename() is no longer transitively included.

Fixes #903

chore(emacs-plus@31): remove fix-basename-macos patch

The upstream fix landed in Emacs master (by Paul Eggert), using pointer
arithmetic instead of basename(). Our temporary workaround patch is no
longer needed.

See: https://debbugs.gnu.org/80224
Closes #903

fix: preserve user PATH ordering in EMACS_PLUS_PATH

Reverse the PATH construction logic: user's PATH now comes first
(preserving their intended order), with missing native comp paths
appended at the end. This fixes tools like dired that rely on
GNU coreutils being found before system binaries.

Fixes #904

fix: derive homebrew prefix dynamically in CaskEnv

Use HOMEBREW_PREFIX constant or environment variable instead of
hardcoding based on CPU architecture. This fixes native compilation
for users with non-standard Homebrew installations.

Fixes #905

feat(community): add fix-macos-tahoe-scrolling patch

Add community patch to fix scrolling lag and input handling issues
on macOS 26 (Tahoe). The patch disables problematic event processing
features via NSUserDefaults.

Based on the emacs-mac patch by Mitsuharu Yamamoto.

Closes #900

feat: promote fix-macos-tahoe-scrolling to built-in patch

Promotes the macOS 26 (Tahoe) scrolling lag fix from community patch
to built-in, applying it unconditionally to all emacs-plus@30 and
emacs-plus@31 builds including cask builds.

The patch disables Apple's undocumented concurrent event processing
(NSEventConcurrentProcessingEnabled, NSApplicationUpdateCycleEnabled)
which interferes with Emacs's NS event loop on Tahoe, causing
scrolling lag and input handling issues.

Based on the equivalent fix in emacs-mac by Mitsuharu Yamamoto.
Tested and confirmed working by lucasec and ToothlessGear.

Closes #900

fix: use compile-time check for Tahoe scrolling patch

Per upstream feedback from Alan Third, replace the runtime version
check with a compile-time preprocessor check using
MAC_OS_X_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED >= 260000.

This follows the standard pattern used in Emacs for macOS
version-specific code.

The comment notes these are undocumented options as of macOS 26.0.

feat: support local file paths for external patches

Allow users to specify local file paths (absolute, ~/home-relative, or
./config-relative) in patch URL fields in build.yml. Relative paths
resolve against the build.yml directory, making configs portable.

Closes #909

chore(emacs-plus@31): drop fix-macos-tahoe-scrolling patch

The fix has been accepted upstream in emacs master:
https://github.com/emacs-mirror/emacs/commit/046f5ef018997e8ef60d2157864ed7d02934d81f
chore: update FUNDING.yml with GitHub Sponsors and Patreon
chore: add sponsor badge and support section to README

fix(emacs-plus@30,31): refresh x-colors during NS window system init

On NS Emacs, x-colors is set by calling ns-list-colors at dump time.
When the dump is created in a headless environment (like CI),
ns-list-colors returns only ~62 colors, while at runtime with a
display it returns the full list (~800+).

This causes packages that rely on x-colors (helm-colors, rainbow-mode,
color-name-rgb-alist, etc.) to see a severely limited color palette.

Fix by refreshing x-colors from ns-list-colors during NS window system
initialization, when the display is available.

Closes #911

fix(emacs-plus@31): remove fix-ns-x-colors patch (merged upstream)

The upstream patch for bug#80377 has been merged into Emacs master,
fixing ns-list-colors to return the full color list at runtime. Our
workaround that refreshed x-colors during NS window system init is no
longer needed for emacs-31. The patch is kept for emacs-30 as the fix
has not been backported.

fix(cask): only remove quarantine xattr instead of clearing all

Replace `xattr -cr` with `xattr -r -d com.apple.quarantine` so that
only the quarantine attribute is removed, preserving other extended
attributes that may be set by security software or other tools.

Closes #920

fix(emacs-plus@30): add explicit version to prevent nil when using custom revision

When a custom revision is set in build.yml, the stable URL is replaced
with a git URL that contains no version information, causing Homebrew to
fail with "invalid attribute for formula: version (nil)".

Adding an explicit version declaration ensures the version is always
defined regardless of URL overrides.

Closes #919

refactor: consolidate version/URL declarations into init

Move version, url, mirror, sha256, and head block setup into
EmacsBase.init so each formula declares version info once:

  init "30.2", sha256: "...", branch: "emacs-30"

This eliminates the redundancy that caused #919 (version nil when
custom revision overrides the stable URL) by always setting an
explicit version. Also adds resolve_revision helper and

find the gcc runtime (libgcc, libemutls_w.a), so on arm64 the test

but still fails on sequoia/tahoe arm64 (newer macOS SDKs). The Homebrew
gcc bottle behind libgccjit bakes in a sysroot; on newer SDKs its JIT
driver can't find the system libraries it links against, so the test
compiles but fails to run. Export SDKROOT from xcrun so the driver uses
the installed SDK, mirroring Homebrew superenv. Also dump config.log on
failure to make any remaining libgccjit linker error visible in CI.

("ld: library 'emutls_w' not found / error invoking gcc driver"). The
previous Cellar-wide `find | head -1` for libemutls_w.a was flaky across
runners (sequoia passed/failed between identical runs). Resolve the dir
via `gcc -print-file-name=libemutls_w.a` (the driver's own mechanism),
hard-fail if absent, and include the libgccjit lib dir on LIBRARY_PATH.

if libemutls_w.a still can't be located.

gcc driver via -print-file-name instead of globbing the Cellar and taking

site-start.el (formula and cask) now appends -L flags for the gcc,
libgccjit and gcc support lib dirs to native-comp-driver-options. Driver

leak into child processes (#939). Paths are resolved at Emacs startup
via gcc -print-file-name, so they survive gcc version bumps without a

fix: don't let one failed cask env step skip the rest (#969)

CaskEnv.inject ran its three steps sequentially, so an exception in an
early one (e.g. the CLI wrapper failing to write) skipped everything
after it, leaving the install partially configured - site-start.el
never patched, client app never recompiled.

Each step now runs through run_step, which reports the failure and
moves on. A failed step counts as needing a re-sign, since it may have
modified the bundle before raising and the cask gates codesign on
inject's return value. The CLI wrapper is also created before the
LSEnvironment already-injected check, so a failed write is retried on
postinstall reruns instead of being skipped forever.

fix: re-sign when only site-start.el changed (#971)

update_site_start_el modifies a file inside the Emacs.app bundle, which
invalidates the code seal just like the plist steps do, but its result
was discarded. On a postinstall rerun where the plist and client marker
are already in place and only a new site-start block gets added, the
cask skipped codesign and left the bundle with a broken seal.

The method now returns whether it wrote the file, and inject counts
that in its needs-resign result.

fix(ci): build tree-sitter from source when there is no Intel bottle

Homebrew treats x86_64 macOS as a tier 3 configuration and no longer
ships bottles for it, so it refuses to build from source unless asked
explicitly. tree-sitter was the first dependency to lose its Intel
bottle, which failed the Install dependencies step in every lane.

tree-sitter is a plain C library with no build dependencies, so the
source build is cheap. The bottle is still tried first, which keeps
arm64 untouched and makes this a no-op if x86_64 bottles come back.

fix(ci): stop a failed Intel build from blocking arm64 releases

One failing matrix leg failed the whole build job, and the release jobs
required it, so a broken Intel build threw away three good arm64 builds
and published nothing. Intel is a tier 3 configuration for Homebrew and
its runner retires in August 2027, so it will keep breaking on its own.

The release jobs now run when a build leg failed, gated on the three
arm64 artifacts being present. Intel is optional: when a run produces no
Intel binary, the cask keeps its own Intel pin on the last release that
did, so the URL always points at an asset that exists. That pin moves
only when there is a fresh Intel binary to move it to.

See #1002 for revisiting Intel support.

fix: update Intel checksums in the casks again

Applying brew style moved the on_intel block below on_arm and put a blank
line between its sha256 and url stanzas. update_cask_sha.py looked for the
checksum on the line directly above the url, so from that point on the
Intel url advanced with every release while its checksum stayed behind,
and cask installs failed verification on Intel. It hit the @next and
@master casks first, then the stable one.

The script now walks back across blank lines and comments to the stanza
that belongs to the url, stops at anything else so it cannot borrow a
neighbouring block's checksum, and exits non-zero when it finds nothing
rather than leaving the old value in place. The release job then verifies
that every checksum it published is present in the cask before committing.

All three casks are corrected to the checksums of the assets their urls
point at.

chore: drop Intel (x86_64) cask builds

Homebrew treats x86_64 macOS as tier 3 and is dropping Intel bottles one
dependency at a time (tree-sitter on 2026-09-01, gcc on 2026-09-03). The
gcc one means a two hour source build on the Intel runner that then
fails for reasons unrelated to Emacs, and it took the release jobs down
with it. Apple ships no new macOS for Intel after Tahoe and GitHub
retires the last x86_64 runner in August 2027, so this is the end of the
road anyway.

The build matrix has no Intel leg, the release jobs no longer treat one
leg as optional, and the casks declare `depends_on arch: :arm64` so an
Intel Mac gets a clear message instead of a missing url. Intel users can
install the formula, which builds from source.

Closes #1002

fix(cask): keep the url outside on_arm so brew tap validates on Intel

Dropping the Intel builds left the cask url only inside on_arm. brew tap
loads every cask on every OS/arch pair before accepting a tap, and on
Intel the casks had no url, so tapping failed with "Invalid cask (macOS N
on intel)" and "invalid syntax in tap". The url now lives at the top
level and depends_on arch: :arm64 is what refuses the install on Intel.

Also drop the verified: url parameter (deprecated in Homebrew 6.0.22) and
replace the bare depends_on :macos with depends_on macos: :sonoma at the
top level (combining the two is disabled in 6.0.22). CI now runs
brew readall --os=all --arch=all so this cannot regress silently.

Closes #1005

refactor(cask): move postflight to postflight_steps

Homebrew 6.0.22 deprecated the postflight and uninstall_postflight
blocks, which will be disabled in a coming release, and its newest cask
cops flag them in every tap. postflight_steps only accepts literal steps
run inside a sandbox, so the Ruby in Library/ now runs through
scripts/cask-postflight as a `run` step, with the build.yml locations
declared so the sandbox lets it read them, and bin/emacs is a `symlink`
step that Homebrew removes on uninstall by itself.

CaskEnv reads and writes plist keys with PlistBuddy instead of
`defaults`, which goes through cfprefsd and is not something to lean on
inside the sandbox. CaskPostflight no longer links bin/emacs; the new
CaskPostflightCLI supplies the system_command it expects and turns
configuration errors into a non-zero exit so the install aborts.

fix(ci): trust the emacs-plus tap before tapping it

Homebrew 7.0.0 stopped treating a bare tap name on the command line as
permission to load that tap's files (Homebrew/brew#23864). brew tap
verifies a tap by loading every formula and cask, so tapping an
untrusted tap now fails with "invalid syntax in tap" and the nightly
trust step never runs. Trust first, then tap, in nightly and validate.
Update the README and release note install snippets the same way.
Emacs 32 scroll crash patch is removed

fix(formula): move post_install to post_install_steps

Homebrew 7.0.0 deprecated the post_install method, and with
HOMEBREW_DEVELOPER=1 (which the nightly builds set) the deprecation is
an error, so every formula failed in the post-install phase while the
build itself succeeded. post_install_steps only accepts literal steps,
so the Ruby now lives in Library/FormulaPostinstall and runs through
scripts/formula-postinstall as a `run` step, with flags that keep each
formula doing what its post_install did: info manuals, the native-lisp
link on 28 and 29, the build.yml icon on 30 and later, and re-signing.

A step cannot know where the tap checkout is and there is no template
token for the Homebrew repository on Intel, so `install` writes a small
launcher into libexec that execs the script from the checkout. That
also keeps `brew postinstall` reading the current Library/ and
community/ files, and works in HOMEBREW_EMACS_PLUS_MODE=local.

chore(cask): sort depends_on stanzas the way Cask/StanzaOrder wants

brew style (Homebrew 7.0.4) flags every depends_on line in the three
casks. The stanza group order was already right (conflicts_with before
depends_on); the cop additionally sorts depends_on stanzas among
themselves by key and value, so the required order is arch, formula
"gcc", formula "libgccjit", macos. The explanatory comments move with
their stanzas. No behaviour change: Homebrew reads all depends_on
stanzas regardless of order.
fix(ci): retry brew install on flaky patch checksums

fix(emacs-plus-app): load bundled site-start.el again

Cask builds passed --enable-locallisppath pointing at Homebrew's
site-lisp (#930). That flag replaces the default site-lisp search path,
which for a self-contained app is the bundle's own site-lisp, so the
bundled site-start.el never loaded. ns-emacs-plus-version was undefined
and the native-comp driver options from #964 never applied, so
terminal launches with a cold eln-cache failed with "ld: library
'emutls_w' not found" (#1016).

Drop the flag and add Homebrew's site-lisp (plus its subdirs.el) to
load-path from site-start.el instead, so mu4e and friends are still
found.

Also seed native-comp-driver-options with Emacs's darwin default
"-Wl,-w" instead of nil, since site-start.el runs before comp.el and
the defcustom keeps whatever value is already bound.

Fixes #1016
